proof.observed: `linger.go` sets `except = claim.RoleImplementer` when `merged` and enqueues the `IssueSuspend` only inside `if !merged`, so a merged close takes five of six claims and queues no suspension; `check.go:261` and `:293` are where a pending look enqueues it. findingsNotFailures.what: Two more sites of the swept prose class, and the fixture asymmetry behind one of them.
findingsNotFailures.evidence: `workflow/merge_close_test.go:215` and `daemon/outbox_issue_suspend_test.go:657` still say a Sandbox is released 'with its volume'. The second sits on `internal/daemon`'s `issueSandbox` helper, which builds `volumeClaimTemplates: [{name: issue}]` for every fixture Sandbox at six sites, where `internal/runtime/sandbox` inverted its own fixture this change: `sandboxObject` owns no template and three sites opt into the old shape with `withSupersededDisk`.
findingsNotFailures.verdict: A finding to fix in this pull request, not a round failure: both are prose, and the fixture is bounded today because those daemon tests suspend and delete rather than launch, so nothing branches on the template. It is worth fixing rather than noting because `supersededDisk()` is true for any issue Sandbox carrying a template — so a daemon test that ever launches into one of these fixtures takes the migration path silently, passes, and proves the wrong thing. One package's fixtures model the world this change makes and the other's model the world it replaces.
